method.note: 60% résumé points / 40% predictive (PR = average of current FPI + SP+ ranks). Résumé points prioritize quality wins, undefeated status, road/Power wins, and penalize losses. Lowest combined score ranks highest. Tiebreakers applied as specified. No brand overrides.

notes.risersFallers:

Editor's note (movement vs. Nov. 1 ranking): Biggest risers: Oregon #20→#9, Tennessee #17→#10, Iowa #25→#19, UCLA #8→#4, Utah #6→#3, Alabama #9→#6. Biggest fallers: LSU #7→#16, Ohio State #5→#12, Missouri #18→#23, Miami #1→#5, Indiana #4→#7. Dropped out: Kentucky (#13), Northwestern (#21), SMU (#24). New: Louisville #21, South Carolina #22, New Mexico #25.
notes.apVsGrok: Grok rates Notre Dame and the two perfect teams (Utah, UCLA) higher than typical human polls because of the résumé weighting and lack of brand inflation. Utah and BYU are treated on merits: Utah’s 9-0 + head-to-head pushes it well above BYU. Other Big 12 teams (Texas Tech #11, Houston #17, Arizona #20) sit where they do on a mix of records and efficiency rather than narrative [editor's correction: source said "in the mid-to-late teens"]. Source projection only (not an actual AP poll): projected AP (from consensus previews) is expected to put Georgia ~1, Utah ~2, Notre Dame ~3, UCLA ~4, Miami ~5 — close at the top but Grok gives more weight to ND’s head-to-head and the perfect records.
notes.nextWeek: Utah at Arizona, UCLA vs. Illinois, Georgia vs. Missouri, and several other ranked/conference games will test the perfect records and the one-loss teams. A loss by Utah or UCLA drops a perfect résumé; continued dominance by Georgia or Notre Dame solidifies the top. Big 12 and Big Ten results will also clarify conference championship paths.
